items.topic: Alphabet (GOOGL/GOOG) Q3 2026 results and -12.6%/-12.3% reaction, dated 2026-10-29
items.facts: Q3 2026 revenue ~$127.6B (+25% YoY, slightly below some estimates); Google Cloud revenue roughly doubled to ~$30.7B with operating income more than tripling. GAAP EPS $2.12 (includes an $8.7B paper loss on equity stakes) vs. adjusted $2.67 against a ~$3.01 consensus. Q3 capex ~$51.4B, more than double a year ago; free cash flow approximately -$9.1B. 2026 capex guidance held at $195-205B; company signaled a significant 2027 step-up, which Fortune estimated at roughly $300B. Shares fell about 10-11% after hours Wednesday; Fortune put the market-value loss at $280B+. Analysts split: some trimmed targets/downgraded, Deutsche Bank kept Buy.
items.caveat: The ~$300B 2027 figure is attributed to one outlet (Fortune), not independently confirmed across sources; reported as such in the brief.

items.topic: ServiceNow (NOW) Q3 2026 results and record -27% drop, dated 2026-10-29
items.facts: Q3 revenue ~$4.11B, roughly in line. Adjusted EPS $1.00 vs. $1.02 consensus. Full-year 2026 subscription revenue guidance lifted slightly to $15.78-15.79B. Remaining performance obligations grew 21% YoY; next-period growth guided toward ~18.5% (deceleration flagged by multiple outlets). TradingKey cited higher interest costs from debt financing the $7.75B Armis acquisition. CNBC: results underwhelmed and reignited AI-disruption-of-enterprise-software concerns. CNBC reported the close as the company's worst single day on record (~27%); premarket figures from other outlets ran lower (18-20%).
items.caveat: Sources disagree on exact drop magnitude (18% premarket vs. 27% at close per CNBC/TradingKey); brief uses the scan's own script-verified close-to-close figure (-26.95%) and cites CNBC's 'worst day on record' characterization as attributed framing, not an independently re-derived stat.

items.topic: Marvell (MRVL) -13.2%, reported Lumentum acquisition talks, dated 2026-10-29
items.facts: Bloomberg reported (per Fool.com/Benzinga) Marvell is in advanced talks to acquire Lumentum, an optical-components maker supplying AI datacenters, in an expected all-stock deal; nothing finalized, announcement possibly as soon as next week. Stock reaction attributed to dilution risk from the all-stock structure plus broader same-day chip weakness (Arm, AMD, Broadcom also down).
items.caveat: Deal unconfirmed/reported, not announced; framed as reported M&A talks, not a completed transaction.

items.topic: AI-datacenter/hyperscaler bond issuance and credit-spread background (weekly Tier 3)
items.facts: Fort Washington (dated this month) estimates >$300B of new AI-related hyperscaler issuance over the trailing 12 months and says concentrated issuance from a few correlated issuers has widened AI-related spreads materially. BlackRock (Aug 12) and Penn Mutual (Aug 6) both describe high-yield data-center spreads widening since June 2026 while investment-grade hyperscaler spreads tightened modestly on scale/relative strength.
items.caveat: None of this is dated to the current week specifically; reported as background context in the weekly Tier 3 section, not a live reading.

items.topic: FOMC Oct 28 decision recap (context for Claims/Story), dated 2026-10-28
items.facts: Fed held target range at 3.75%-4.00%, a 10-2 vote; Lisa Cook (Board governor) and Beth Hammack (Cleveland Fed President) dissented for a hike. Chair Kevin Warsh at the press conference.
items.caveat: Consistent with 2026-10-29 brief's own correction (Hammack is a Reserve Bank president, not a governor); carried forward correctly here.
